Yes, it should work for normal videos, likely not 4k@60Hz though.

You could use the Pi as storage node or also as "media center" as long as you don't try too fancy stuff.

This is definitely possible. I'm running Kodi (formerly known as XBMC) on my Pi2, and it runs just fine.

Streaming from the internet, AirPlay over my network, loaded on a USB/external HD... it all plays great. It's good for YouTube videos, Pandora radio, and content I physically have and don't want to stream.

The only problem that you're going to run into is with an external HD: The Rasbperry platform (regardless of which you use) pulls a maximum of 2.5A for the entire system, including all of your USB devices and the processor. So, if you have an external HD attached to the Pi, it's going to either have to be self-powered or you're going to need a powered hub for the HD to properly spin up. If you don't do this, the HD will never receive the proper power and it'll never mount to the system.

I personally have a 16GB USB stick that I load media onto as I want to enjoy them, kind of like the way you would load music onto an iPod before going out for a run/yardwork. I'll either load my media directly to the USB physically, or I'll copy it over my network and load it either onto the USB or the SD card installed in the Pi. I just don't have a need to buy a powered hub and use an entire HD with all of my media.
I used a NAS attached to the same switch and mounted to the rasplex, and it worked pretty well. It was fast, and there was no draw on the power from the pi.

This! Exactly this! All of my Pi2 home theater setups use OSMC which comes with a very easy and intuitive setup process. The only problem I've ever had with it is that for still as of yet unknown reasons it won't automatically mount certain disks, but this is easily and permanently fixed by adding the disk yourself in the /etc/fstab file.

Once installed, OSMC can then share the media over a network via Zeroconf, AirPlay, upnp, and Samba (Windows file sharing). Any other computer on the network can then use a program like Kodi to connect back to the pi server with the HDD attached and watch movies on that device, streamed from the Pi's HDD.
